note: Wall-pilot rules of the fast race-cue pilot inside the obstacle stack (visual_brain --obstacle-stack on|shadow; off by default and outside the stack; --wall-pilot off removes them from the stack). 'turn_first': haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.TurnFirstConfig, turn before translating at a wall when the next checkpoint is far off the heading (a hairpin). 'ceiling_guard': haltere.liftoff.fast_race_cue.CeilingGuardConfig, keep the looming TTC governor's terrain climb out of ceilings and overhangs. Generic and course-agnostic: they read only the pilot's own state, the causal looming samples and the visible checkpoint marker. The values are a-priori (the M2 round-2 task values: stand-off or a wall brake below about 1.5 m/s, a bearing beyond about 45-60 deg, a request of at most 0.5-1 m/s, a climb of about 1 m/s without persistent below-path evidence), set after inspecting the three Minus Two incidents they address (minus-brain08-gapon-01/02 ceiling, minus-fast6-gapon-01 hairpin side push); version 1 was frozen before any replay of these rules; versions 2 and 3 each add one condition to the overhead cut after an open-loop replay of the previous version (see change and previous_versions), so the Minus Two incident replays and the Straw Bale quietness replays are development evidence for version 3, not held-out evidence. The runner refuses another version (fast_race_cue.WALL_PILOT_VERSION). The hash covers everything except frozen/frozen_at/sha256; a change needs a new version and a new freeze before any live flight, and every version flown is reported. Offline replays of these rules are open loop and are not flight evidence.

turn_first_notes.condition: near a wall: the TTC governor holds a stand-off (a wall sample capped the request at standoff_speed, 2 m/s, or less within standoff_s), or its wall brake capped the request within brake_recent_s while the horizontal speed is at most slow_speed; and the checkpoint marker is clamped at a side edge or corner (pilot state 'side'), or its filtered bearing (in view, or clamped at the bottom/top edge away from the corners) is engage_deg or more off the heading. The camera's horizontal half field of view is about 58 deg (focal_320 100 px), so 50 deg is a marker near the image edge
turn_first_notes.action: the horizontal request loses its component toward the wall (the horizontal part of the looming ray that capped the request, taken at engagement) and is bounded to creep_speed; the request's speed toward the wall is removed at the clearance brake_slew (15 m/s^2); the vertical request and the yaw rule are unchanged, so the assisted yaw keeps turning toward the checkpoint
turn_first_notes.release: aligned: the bearing of a marker in view (or bottom/top clamped) is within release_deg of the heading (the declared cone; the ordinary speed schedule and acceleration limits then resume); handoff: search, launch or a support climb owns the request; timeout: max_s after engagement, then no new episode for rearm_s, so the drone never hovers at a wall indefinitely

ceiling_guard_notes.unexplained_alarms: without the guard a sample without vertical evidence (below_fraction None: one of looming2's vertical windows has no evidence, or neither is urgent) counts as terrain while a climb is active. On minus-brain08-gapon-01 the alarms from the garage ceiling ahead of the climbing path (TTC 0.93 -> 0.43 s, below_fraction None, lower TTC none or 1.23 s) raised the climb from 0.4 to 3.5 m/s. With the guard such a sample is terrain only when the lower window explains it (lower TTC <= lower_ratio x alarm TTC), otherwise a wall
ceiling_guard_notes.weak_climb: a climb from such an explained sample (terrain seen by the lower window only) requests at most weak_climb (the task's ~1 m/s), refreshes the climb hold only at that level, and is ignored weak_climb_max_m above where the last below-path climb request (below_fraction >= terrain_fraction) was accepted; below-path climbs keep the TTC policy's vertical_up and climb_max_m
ceiling_guard_notes.overhead: during a climb (or an overhead hold), while the measured vertical speed exceeds overhead_min_rise, a sample with alarm TTC < overhead_ttc_s (the TTC policy's climb_on_s) whose expansion lies above the path (below_fraction <= overhead_fraction) or is unexplained is overhead evidence; overhead_confirm of them within the governor's confirm_window_s (0.25 s), at least overhead_positive of them positive (see overhead_positive), cut the climb to 0 and start an overhead hold of hold_s, renewed by further confirmed evidence: no terrain climb, below-path samples brake like walls (terrain_brake 0 would otherwise let rising ground pass unbraked), and the whole vertical request (pilot and governor) is bounded to vertical_cap (level) and brought down at vertical_slew m/s^2 (the clearance brake_slew) instead of the pilot's 5 m/s^2. Level flight is unaffected: overhead evidence only counts during a climb or a hold, and only while the drone rises
ceiling_guard_notes.not_used: looming2 already fits an 'up' window 0.12 W above the focus of expansion (ttc_upper, report only). It is not published by the camera process and the live logs do not carry it; while climbing, that window lies at the top of the image, where the HUD mask removes the upper 20 % (on gapon-01 at 18.5 s the lower window was urgent while below_fraction was None, so the upper window had no evidence under the ceiling). The guard therefore uses the fields the camera already publishes
ceiling_guard_notes.overhead_min_rise: a ceiling or overhang can only cross a rising flight path; an alarm ahead of a level or sinking path is braked for as a wall and does not stop a climb that arrests a sink. 0.3 m/s is a noise margin on the measured vertical speed, not fitted
ceiling_guard_notes.overhead_positive: a sample is positive overhead evidence when something shows that the alarm is not the surface below the path: below_fraction <= overhead_fraction (the expansion lies above the path), or a lower-surface TTC that is known and longer than lower_ratio x the alarm TTC. A sample in which neither vertical window crosses the path (below_fraction None and lower TTC None) says nothing either way: climbing a hill, both windows often lose it. Such samples still count toward overhead_confirm but cannot confirm alone. On gapon-02 the confirming sample had below_fraction 0.0; on gapon-01 the ceiling alarms included a lower TTC of 1.23 s against an alarm of 0.63 s

change: v3 (after the open-loop Straw Bale quietness replay of v2 with offline looming samples, before any flight): the overhead cut also needs at least overhead_positive (1) positive sample. In the v2 replay of the clean laps straw-brain08-04 and -06 it fired 7 times, each time during a hill climb on two samples in which neither vertical window crossed the path (below_fraction None, lower TTC None, alarm TTC 0.8-1.2 s); the laps were flown without any climb, but on a mound the same pattern would cut a needed climb. Every other value and rule is version 2's.
